reference_sql:
SELECT LOWER(TRIM(category_raw)) AS spelling, COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM products
WHERE category_id = 2
GROUP BY 1
alternatives:
WITH spellings AS (  -- one row per product of category 2
  SELECT LOWER(TRIM(category_raw)) AS spelling
  FROM products
  WHERE category_id = 2
)
SELECT spelling, COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM spellings
GROUP BY spelling
SELECT TRIM(LOWER(category_raw)) AS spelling, COUNT(*) AS n_products FROM products WHERE category_id = 2 GROUP BY TRIM(LOWER(category_raw))

other_way.sql:
WITH spellings AS (  -- one row per product of category 2
  SELECT LOWER(TRIM(category_raw)) AS spelling
  FROM products
  WHERE category_id = 2
)
SELECT spelling, COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM spellings
GROUP BY spelling
other_way.tradeoff: A named step cleans each spelling once and groups by its name, which reads well, but the grouped query is shorter.
